text: Version control is essential for modern software development, and Git is its most popular tool. A key concept is branching, which lets you work on new ideas without disrupting the main codebase. Instead of editing the main line directly, you create a feature branch. This is like a separate workspace where you can experiment, fix bugs, or develop new functions safely. Once your work is complete and tested, you merge that branch back into the main branch. In team settings, this often happens through a pull request, where others review your changes before merging. This workflow keeps the main version stable, encourages collaboration, and makes it easy to track what was changed and why.
